title: The morphism given by a bijective reordering of the coordinate sections is invertible
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\beta,\gamma$ be coordinate types, and let $b:\gamma\simeq\beta$ be an equivalence. Write $X=\mathbb P(\beta;S)$ [def-pc-proj], $M=(\operatorname{id}_X)^*\mathcal O_X(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-projective-space-twist], $s_j=(\operatorname{id}_X)^*T_{b(j)}$, and $U_j=D_+(T_{b(j)})$. The morphism $\phi:X\to\mathbb P(\gamma;S)$ constructed by the native homOfIsFreeGenerator from the sections $s_j$, their free-generator witnesses on $U_j$, and the cover $\bigcup_j U_j=X$, over the structure morphism $X\to S$, is an isomorphism. No finiteness or nonemptiness assumption on the coordinate types is required.

source.place: Constructions Definition 01NF and Lemma 01NE: projective-space charts and coordinate construction, applied to bijective renaming and its inverse.

proof.text: The native homOfIsFreeGenerator_appLE_coordRatio sends T_j/T_i to the coefficient of s_j relative to s_i. Apply pullbackSection_twistOneSection_map_eq_smul to the identity morphism and use uniqueness of the coefficient of a free generator. The coefficient is T_(b j)/T_(b i). Thus on the standard chart indexed by b i, the morphism is the affine coordinate reindexing from variables other than i to variables other than b i. For an arbitrary base S, standardOpenIso identifies these charts with relative affine spaces. Restrict over an affine open Spec R of S before referring to polynomial coordinate rings; homOfIsFreeGenerator_over ensures that the map fixes R. These affine base opens cover S.

The bijection b restricts to a bijection between these sets of variables. The polynomial rename equivalence and its inverse give mutually inverse affine chart morphisms. Their restrictions to intersections agree: both maps replace each coordinate ratio by the ratio with its two indices renamed. They therefore glue; alternatively use the existing native homOfIsFreeGenerator construction for b.symm to define the inverse.

On every standard chart the composites of these maps fix the base and every affine coordinate, since b.symm (b j) = j and b (b.symm i) = i. The affine-space hom_ext theorem makes these chart composites identities. Equality on the covering standard charts makes the global composites identities. Therefore phi is an isomorphism. When the coordinate types are empty, the schemes have the empty standard cover, and the same covering equality proves the claim.
